title: Anticipatory capacity runway review — week of 2028-10-15
content:
Meeting: Anticipatory Capacity Runway Review
Date: 2028-10-15 09:30 PT
Attendees: Liam, Priya, Noah, Evelyn, Samir, Anya (SRE), Marcus (Product)
Objective: Validate regional buffer plans for H2-Q4 traffic tails, decide prewarming schedule for holiday promotions, triage an observed priming regression in APAC edge clusters.

High-level summary:
- Current fleet headroom is healthy but skewed: global buffer 16% overall; US-west-heavy (22% buffer), EU-central marginal (9%), APAC low (3%).
- Observed uptick in short-lived interactive sessions from two high-volume customers (traffic spike pattern: 30–60s bursts, high concurrency) which increases tail latency and reduces effective capacity.
- Prewarming experiment v3 improved first-token latency for H100 pools by median 120ms in controlled trials, but increased cost by ~8% (measured as per-token GPU time).
- Action: short-term region-specific prewarming, plus an APAC capacity hedging step (cross-region spillover policy) to run for 3 weeks while procuring spot H100s.

Operational observations & metrics (last 7 days):
- Total active GPUs: A100-40GB: 1,120, H100-80GB: 560, L4: 260 (inference optimized).
- Global average utilization (7d): 62% (tokens/sec normalized).
- P95 request latency (gen): US-W: 142ms, EU-C: 198ms, APAC-SG: 254ms.
- Spot eviction events: 12 (mostly EU-C preemptible pool), leading to 4 small customer-facing errors (auto-retry handled).
- Cache hit rate (prefix/KV) for long-running chat sessions: 47% global; APAC: 36% (lower due to ephemeral sessions).

Region-specific notes:
- US-West (us-west1):
  - Buffer: 22% (above target).
  - Plan: keep current autoscale bands; disable additional prewarming except for 3 tagged customers with observed 3x burst patterns.
  - Risk: none immediate.

- EU-Central (eu-central1):
  - Buffer: 9% (below preferred 15%).
  - Observed: increased spot eviction rate due to provider maintenance windows.
  - Plan: shift low-priority Dedicated pods to alternate instance families; run targeted pre-warm during 06:00–10:00 UTC; submit procurement request for 48 additional H100 hours/week.
  - Action owner: Priya (runbook update + procurement ticket).

- APAC-SG (apac-sg1):
  - Buffer: 3% (critical).
  - Observed: priming regression in stateless prewarm v2 -> v3 migration (long tail of cold starts for L4-backed edge pools).
  - Root cause hypothesis: priming job scheduler collision with short-lived batch teardown; warmed KV caches being evicted by autoscaler policy sooner than expected.
  - Short-term mitigation: enable cross-region spillover to us-west1 for tagged enterprise customers during business hours (UTC+8 00:00–12:00), bump min-replicas for edge L4 pools from 1 -> 2.
  - Long-term: dedicate a small reserved L4 mini-pool in APAC (proposal: 20 L4s for peak 4 weeks) — Action owner: Noah (capacity request).

Prewarming and priming experiments recap:
- Experiment v3 (stateless priming, keep-alive buckets):
  - Result: median cold-start reduction 120ms for H100, 80ms for A100; cost increase ~8% in per-token GPU time due to idle prewarm durations.
  - Tradeoff: better latency SLO adherence vs higher $/token.
  - Decision: roll v3 in regions with buffer >= 15% (US-W), run controlled partial rollout in EU-C during low-demand windows, postpone APAC rollout until pool stability confirmed.

Capacity runway and procurement ask:
- Target runway for Q4 promotional tail: maintain 18% global buffer with regional floor 12% except for short-lived exceptions for APAC (target 8% while hedging).
- Procurement request (submitted INFRA-2248): 48 H100 hours/week (on-demand/reserved mix) for EU-C, and 20 L4 reserved nodes in APAC for 4 weeks (proof-of-efficacy period).
- Financial estimate: incremental incremental monthly cost delta ~ $72k if spot discount not available; expected to drop to $30k/mo after autoscaler tuning and cache improvements.

Risk register (top items):
1) APAC priming instability — impact: degraded p95 and customer errors; mitigation: min-replicas bump + cross-region spill; contingency: failover to dedicated us-west routing.
2) Spot eviction cluster in EU -> cascading queue growth -> elevated latency; mitigation: move critical backfills off spot, preemptive eviction window awareness.
3) Cost creep from prewarming if adopted globally; mitigation: region gating + per-customer rollout thresholds + telemetry-based auto-disable.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Product: Accept temporary cross-region routing for enterprise customers (Marcus) — decision required by 2028-10-18.
- Finance: Approve one-month reserved L4 pool for APAC to stabilize latency while procurement completes. Estimate required: ticket submitted, need sign-off.
- SRE: Confirm scheduled maintenance in eu-central for 2028-10-21 (expected spot churn).

Action items (owners & ETA):
- Priya: open procurement / budget ticket for EU H100 hours; update EU runbook to reflect alternate families (ETA 2028-10-17).
- Noah: submit reservation request for 20 L4s in APAC and update autoscaler config to bump min-replicas for edge pools (ETA 2028-10-18).
- Evelyn: run controlled v3 rollout in EU-C (canary 10% traffic) and capture latency/cost delta; if p95 improves without >10% cost increase, expand (ETA 2028-10-20).
- Samir: create a short-lived dashboard showing per-customer burst pattern heatmaps and KV cache retention metrics (ETA 2028-10-19).
- Liam: draft customer-facing note for the two affected customers offering mitigation and asking consent for cross-region routing (send by 2028-10-17).

Notes to self / rough ideas (brainstorm fragments):
- Consider a predictive priming scheduler tied to customer session forecasting (model run on usage history) to reduce idle prewarm time.
- Explore micro-reservations (reserve tiny capacity slabs for specific high-lambda customers) rather than bulk prewarming.
- Could we implement a short-lived KV pinning policy (TTL extension) for primed caches while auto-scaler detects recent warms?

Next sync: short status update 2028-10-18 10:00 PT (target final decisions on cross-region routing and APAC reservation).

Appendix: quick logs / links
- Tail sample (example cold-start stacktrace snippet): GCE instance reclaim -> docker SIGTERM -> priming job timeout -> request reroute.
- Helpful links: INFRA runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INFRA/Priming+Runbook, procurement ticket: JIRA INFRA-2248, priming PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/fleet-scripts/pull/312

End of notes.
